chunk_findings.detail: The detached run clears the wire marker only in the `finally` around `BS.baseline_for`. If the caller has already created the marker before invoking this entry point—as the cleanup here implies—any early return or exception before the `try` leaves it behind. For example, if the marker is created and then this process runs after the `unit_tests` command has changed, the check at line 78 (`gdef.command != command`) returns 2 without unlinking; the marker file remains, so baseline_wire can keep believing a detached measurement is still running.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/baseline_measure.py:91

chunk_findings.detail: The write path treats `failing` as authoritative when an id appears in both `Measured.failures` and `Measured.flaky`: it stores `"tests": failing` and `"flaky": sorted(got.flaky - set(failing))`. For the natural flaky case where a test failed under the full run but passed alone, a measurement can represent that as `failures={"t": ...}` and `flaky={"t"}`. Given that input, `record` writes `t` into the known-red `tests` map and omits it from the `flaky` list, so the gate will still treat `t` as a known-red failure, contrary to the new docstring/intent that failures passing alone are flaky and never among the failing ids.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/baseline_store.py:145 (`record`)

chunk_findings.detail: The single-flight marker is checked and written non-atomically around `jobs.launch`. Given `[baseline].measure = "auto"` and no complete record, two concurrent `compare` calls for the same `(repo, sha, command)` can both see `BS.load` incomplete and `_marker_pid` return 0, then both launch detached `baseline_measure`; the second `atomic_write` overwrites the first pid. If the second run exits before the first, a later call sees a dead pid and launches a third run while the first is still running. Likewise, if `atomic_write` fails after `jobs.launch` succeeds (disk full, marker path a directory, etc.), `start_measure` returns `failed` even though a detached run is already running and the marker is absent, enabling another duplicate. This violates the documented “single-flight per sha ... two lanes at one sha start one run” and can duplicate expensive measurements or race the shared log/store.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/baseline_wire.py:start_measure

chunk_findings.detail: The `source` knob declares `off` as the strictest value, but `off` is not stricter than `recorded` in the scenario this change is meant to prevent. Suppose a unit_tests branch forked from main before main introduced a new failure in test `T`, and the branch itself also fails `T` with the same failure signature. With `source=recorded`, the gate compares against the fork point, where `T` is not in the recorded known-red set, so `T` is a new failure and the branch fails. With `source=off`, the gate runs `T` on main's moved tip, sees it fail there, treats it as baseline-red, and lets the branch pass. Thus a configuration that selects the declared strictest value can be more permissive than the default and can excuse a failure introduced after the fork point, contrary to the stated intent that gates not judge against main's moved tip.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/baseline.py:source

chunk_findings.detail: `_load` accepts a pre-existing cached entry as valid even though this change altered both the meaning of a complete entry and the digest calculation. It returns `flaky=()` whenever the stored JSON lacks the new `flaky` key, and `baseline_for` will not re-measure a fresh `complete` entry. For example, an old local store file with `{"sha": "...", "complete": true, "measured_at": fresh, "tests": {"test_x": "<old digest>"}}` is loaded as `Baseline(failing={"test_x": old_digest}, flaky=())`. If `test_x` now passes when run alone, the new policy would classify it as flaky and not known-red, but the gate still sees it in `failing` and passes it. The same stale-entry problem applies to digest normalization: a stored old digest containing a memory address will no longer match `digest_of` after this change. The store should invalidate or re-measure entries that predate the flaky/digest semantics (e.g. via a format/version marker or requiring the `flaky` key).
chunk_findings.title: baseline_store._load

chunk_findings.detail: `start_measure` can start two detached measurements for the same `(sha, command)` when replacing a dead marker. Concrete interleaving: two lanes see the same old dead marker. Lane B passes `_held`, unlinks the old marker, then its next `_claim` succeeds and it breaks (or is preempted just before/at launch), creating a new marker. Lane A had already evaluated `_held` on the old marker and now reaches `path.unlink(missing_ok=True)` at line 240; this unconditionally deletes B's newly created marker, so A's next `_claim` also succeeds. Both lanes then launch `baseline_measure`, violating the single-flight-per-sha guarantee and potentially running two concurrent measurements that can contend on the same store/log paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/baseline_wire.py:start_measure

chunk_findings.detail: `test_ci_is_judged_at_the_tip_it_merges_and_unit_tests_at_the_fork` calls `BW.base_of("ci", repo, tree, "main")` with four positional arguments, but `base_of` in `baseline_wire.py` only accepts three parameters (`repo, tree, main_ref`). Given this call, Python raises a `TypeError: base_of() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given`, causing the test suite to crash immediately on execution.
